name: Separate header loading states so only one spinner shows at a time
description: The Refresh, Update branch, and Create PR/Push buttons all read the shared app.push state, distinguished only by the coarse intent field. Any pull-shaped op (pull, update-from-default, upstream sync) set intent=pull and lit up multiple buttons at once; the Create PR/Push button spun for ANY in-progress op; and every op trailing refresh flipped the loading flags that spin the Refresh icon. This adds a precise op discriminator so each header button spins only for its own work — never two header spinners at once.

steps.title: Add a precise op discriminator to push state
steps.body: `intent` (push | pull | stash-restore) drives conflict-dialog routing and is too coarse for spinner attribution — pull, update-from-default and upstream-sync all share intent `pull`. New `op` field maps 1:1 to the user-facing action that owns the operation, so the header can attribute the spinner to exactly one button. Every place that assigns `app.push` now sets `op`: pull/confirmStashAndPull→`pull`, updateFromDefault→`update`, updateFromUpstream→`update-upstream`, push/fork/abort→`push`, commit/undo→`commit`, stash restores→`stash-restore`. `intent` is left untouched so ConflictDialog still works.

callouts.body: The new field. `op` is purely for header spinner attribution; `intent` keeps its conflict-routing meaning.

steps.title: Refresh button: spin only for its own pull / standalone refresh
steps.body: The Pull affordance now keys on `op === pull` instead of `intent === pull`, so an update-branch or upstream sync no longer spins it. The refresh-icon spinner is gated on `!app.push.inProgress`: while any push-state op owns the header its own button spins, and the refreshFiles/refreshBranches it runs on completion would otherwise flip the same loading.files/branches flags and light a second spinner here. The button still disables during any op so a fetch can not be stacked on a push/update.

steps.title: Update branch button: spin only for update-from-default
steps.body: Was `intent === pull`, which also matched a plain pull and an upstream sync. Now `op === update`, set solely by updateFromDefault — the action this button triggers.

steps.title: Create PR / Push button: spin only for its own push
steps.body: Previously `busy` was `inProgress && stage !== conflicts` — it spun for ANY operation (pull, update, commit), which is the most visible form of the bug: clicking Update branch made the Create PR button spin even though openPRPage just opens a URL and does no push work. Now `busy` requires `op === push`. Disabling is split out from spinning: the button still locks during ANY in-flight git op, but only spins for its own push/publish.

callouts.body: Disable (lock during any op) is now separate from busy (spin only for own op) — so the button can be disabled without showing a phantom spinner.
